intro.title: Build heartbeat and presence client logic
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a client-side heartbeat and presence system for a web application. You will learn to use JavaScript's setInterval and clearInterval functions to send periodic signals (heartbeats) to a server, indicating that a user is active and online. The core programming concept involves managing state and side effects to track user presence over time. You will implement this by creating a function that starts a timer to send heartbeat requests and another to stop it, using fetch for network communication. This will help you understand how real-time applications maintain live user status updates.
intro.usecase: Heartbeat and presence logic is essential for any application that needs to track user activity and connection status in real-time. For example, collaborative tools like Google Docs or Figma use it to show live cursors and avatars of other active users, while chat applications like Slack or Discord display online/offline status indicators. As a developer, implementing this pattern is key for building interactive dashboards, multiplayer games, or live support systems where knowing who is connected and active directly impacts the user experience.
